jobs.title: Director of Finance And Accounting
jobs.description:
Director of Finance / Director of Accounting | Vancouver & Lower Mainland
Location:
Vancouver, BC and surrounding Lower Mainland
Employment:
Permanent and Contract Opportunities
Compensation:
Typically $150,000 to $210,000+ annually, depending on experience and opportunity

The Opportunity
Torus Talent is connecting with senior finance and accounting leaders across British Columbia as we continue to develop our executive and senior management talent network.
We are interested in speaking with experienced Directors of Finance, Directors of Accounting, Senior Controllers, and other accomplished finance professionals who are considering their next leadership opportunity.

Our clients operate across a range of industries, including manufacturing, distribution, mining, technology, professional services, and other commercial sectors.
We are particularly interested in individuals who combine strong technical accounting expertise with commercial awareness, strategic thinking, and a proven ability to lead and develop finance teams.

Typical Responsibilities
Depending on the organization and mandate, responsibilities may include:
Providing leadership and strategic direction across finance and accounting functions.
Overseeing financial reporting, accounting operations, and regulatory compliance.
Leading annual budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and performance analysis.
Partnering with the CFO, CEO, and executive leadership on financial and operational strategy.
Developing financial policies, internal controls, and governance frameworks.
Managing cash flow, working capital, and financial risk.
Leading and mentoring Controllers, Accounting Managers, FP&A professionals, and accounting teams.
Supporting mergers, acquisitions, integrations, and business transformation initiatives.
Overseeing ERP implementations, financial systems, and process improvements.
Presenting financial results, business insights, and recommendations to executive leadership and stakeholders.
Supporting long-term financial planning and organizational growth.

Qualifications and Experience
We are interested in senior professionals who offer:
A CPA designation, with additional finance qualifications considered an asset.
10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience.
Previous leadership experience as a Director of Finance, Director of Accounting, Corporate Controller, or similar.
Demonstrated success leading and developing accounting and finance teams.
Strong technical knowledge of ASPE, IFRS, and/or US GAAP.
Experience with financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and executive reporting.
A proven ability to partner with senior leadership on strategic and operational decisions.
Experience managing complex financial structures, multiple business units, or international operations.
Strong commercial judgment, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Experience in private equity-backed, high-growth, multi-entity, or publicly traded organizations would be particularly relevant.

Why Connect With Torus Talent?
At this level, finding the right opportunity involves alignment between leadership style, business strategy, organizational culture, and long-term career objectives.
Our team works with organizations seeking experienced finance leaders who can strengthen financial operations, support business growth, and contribute at the executive level.
We welcome confidential conversations with established finance leaders who are actively considering a move or would like to remain informed about future opportunities.

Interested in discussing your next leadership opportunity?

Submit your resume to join our senior finance and accounting talent network. Our team will contact you to better understand your experience, career interests, and the types of opportunities that may be relevant.

jobs.title: Director of finance
jobs.description:
REPORT TO: Head of School

POSITION GROUP: Senior Leadership Team

STATUS: Full-Time, Permanent

At Calgary French & International School (CFIS), exceptional education is supported by strong leadership, responsible stewardship, and a commitment to excellence. As we experience significant enrolment growth and campus expansion, we are seeking a strategic, forward-thinking Director of Finance
to help guide our financial sustainability and future development.

Guided by our values of We Care, We Connect, We Strive, and We Grow
, CFIS is a collaborative and ambitious school community. The Director of Finance will be a key member of our leadership team, bringing financial expertise, sound judgment, and strategic insight to support informed decision-making and responsible growth.

Anticipated Start Date:
December 1, 2026, or a mutually agreeable date for the successful candidate.

Purpose of the Position

CFIS’s Director of Finance will be a self-motivated, methodical and conscientious leader. The successful candidate will be a key contributor to the strategic plan and strategic financial plan, will ensure the financial health of the school and the feasibility of strategic decisions, and will support financial activities to allow the school’s Board of Directors to meet its fiscal responsibilities. They will oversee the operations of the school’s Finance and Human Resources Departments, and as such will lead, coach and manage two direct reports for high performance. 
The Director of Finance will be a member of the Senior Leadership Team and will work closely with the Head of School, Assistants Head of School and Departmental Directors.

Job Responsibilities: 

The position’s key responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:
Prepare quarterly financial statements and variance analyses for the CFIS Society.
Implement and maintain effective financial policies and procedures to ensure financial integrity.
Provide senior leadership team with monthly departmental/divisional financial reports.
Work closely with senior leadership team and provide financial leadership and strategic insight to the Head of School.  
Lead and coach the Finance and Human Resources Departments to ensure that the department’s stakeholders see the departments as an operational partner in achieving their goals.
Business planning, budget development, and performance measurement.
Preparation of financial information for Alberta Education’s Annual Education Results Report and Three-Year Business Plan, and Annual Operating Plan.
Preparation of annual T3010 Registered Charity Information Return.
In collaboration with the Head of School and senior leadership team, prepare annual budget and financial strategic plan for the CFIS Society.
Maintain internal control system to support the growth and expansion of CFIS.
Lead the Business Office through the year-end external financial audit and any other financial audits by government bodies.
Lead, oversee, and evaluate the business units of the school’s operations and ensure appropriate process mapping, planning, organization, leadership, performance management, and accountability.
Annual issuance of childcare tax receipts.
Monthly issuance of charitable tax receipts and gift-in-kind tax receipts.
Verify and ensure bank covenant calculations on a quarterly basis.
Ensure compliance with Alberta Education’s Level 2 funding requirements and reporting.
Review the Finance and HR Department’s processes, technology and departmental structure to harness the benefits of automation, process modernization and finance effectiveness best practices. 
Continue to ensure the full integration of all business transactions and the accounting system. 
Prepare input for and analyze results of the CAIS benchmarking report.
Attend monthly meetings of the CFIS Society’s Board of Directors and Finance & Audit Committee. 

Qualifications : 

The ideal candidate will bring the following education, experience, skills and competencies:
A university degree from a recognized post-secondary institution and a Chartered Professional Accountant designation (or equivalent).
A minimum of ten years of progressively responsible experience in accounting, audit procedures, and financial operations.
A minimum of three years of experience leading a finance function or a team of at least five.
Demonstrated impact in non-profit or business organizations in a senior leadership position.
Extensive knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), consolidation theory and practice, modern controllership, financial and accounting theories and practices, in order to ensure the appropriate financial framework of the school, provide specialized financial expertise, advice and leadership, and to set accounting standards and ensure compliance.
Ability to present complex financial information to various audiences, and present convincing recommendations for effective and appropriate financial management. 
Solid analytical, organization, planning and problem-solving capabilities.
Able to think both strategically and tactically.
Excellent attention to detail.
Excellent communication skills, preferably in both English and French (English essential).

The successful candidate will need to provide, or have on file, an updated Police Information Check with Vulnerable Sector Screening prior to commencing work. 

Skills, Technical and Behavioural Competencies Required: 

Preference will be given to candidates who:
Are strong planners and organizers.
Have previous experience with non-profit financial management and operations.
Model best practices of exemplary professionalism in dealing with all stakeholders.
Possess strong interpersonal skills that foster collegiality and further the common goals of CFIS’s mission, vision and values.
Have previous experience working in an independent school.
Have experience with finance automation and process modernization. Sage 300 is the school’s current accounting platform.
Experience in the role of Chief Financial Officer in a not-for-profit organization would be beneficial.

Compensation:

We offer a competitive, comprehensive salary and benefits package as well as opportunities for professional growth.
Our benefits include:
Personal days
Sick days
Retirement Savings Benefit
60% tuition discount for children of full-time employees
Extended health and dental coverage
Health and Wellness Spending Accounts
Three weeks paid vacation time off in addition to two-weeks off at winter break and one-week off at March break when the school is closed.

Pay range:
$160,000 to $180,000 annual salary based on education and experience.

Application Process:

This job posting will remain open until filled.
If this position sounds like the perfect fit for you, please submit your cover letter and resume to Apply Now
. Don’t meet every single requirement? At CFIS we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role, but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway with a cover letter and resume describing why you are a great fit and to help us learn more about you. You may be just the right candidate! 

We thank all applicants in advance for their submission.

jobs.title: Assistant to the Director of Finance (Part Time),  Diocese of Rupert’s Land
jobs.description:
Overview

The Assistant to the Director of Finance administers Payroll and Benefits, Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Donation Database, and Third Party Liability Insurance, in accordance with the policies and procedures established by the Synod and the Bishop. Serving as a member of the Diocesan office team located in Winnipeg, the role is accountable to the Director of Finance.

Responsibilities

Financial Stewardship and Administration

Administers payroll and benefit programs for the Diocesan centralized payroll
Ensures all Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and applicable minimum Employment Standards regulations are met
Prepares Accounts Receivable
Prepares Accounts Payable
Reconciles Payroll, Accounts Receivable, and Accounts Payable accounts
Maintains donation database and issues donation receipts
Liaises between parishes and insurer in regards to third party liability insurance
Fosters a positive work environment and provides human resources related support within the position’s scope of responsibility

Parish Support

Serves as a resource to parishes including clergy and lay leaders and their staff in such financial and human resource administration areas as, but not limited to:
Fulfillment of CRA regulations, employment standards and regulations
Safety legislation
Insurance coverage
National Church pension and benefits program
Privacy legislation
Diocesan and National Church policies, procedures, programs and services
Communicates with parishes of all clergy salary and benefits changes
Monitors receipts of parish contributions to the Diocese and keeps parishes advised of the status of their account
Nurtures positive relationships with all stakeholders

Other related duties as assigned

Required Qualifications
Working towards Chartered Professional Accountant designation in Manitoba
A Certified Public Accountant or equivalent from originating country
Must be able to legally work in Canada
Demonstrated knowledge of payroll and benefits administration including all CRA regulations
Extensive  experience utilizing accounting/financial related software
Strong skills in Microsoft Office products, with an excellent knowledge of Excel
Detail oriented and resourceful
Demonstrated excellence of inter-personal, relationship building, customer service and communication skills (oral and written), and goodwill
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively as part of a team
Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgement, prioritize work, maintain confidentiality, and make independent decisions within the parameters of the job description
Basic knowledge of systems administration
Availability to work occasional evenings and weekends including attendance at designated events

Additional Skills (desired, but not required)
Experience with Payworks
Familiarity with accounting software (Account Edge)
Experience working with Not For Profit Organizations
Knowledge of the administrative structure of the Anglican Church of Canada

Work Parameters
A part time position (8 hrs/day, 3 days a week), competitive salary, with benefit plans including pension, extended health, and continuing education

Please submit your applications to finance@rupertsland.ca.

DEADLINE FOR SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS IS NOVEMBER 15 2026.

jobs.title: Director Data Platform Governance
jobs.description:
Director Data Platform Governance
Toronto, Canada (Hybrid)
Full Time

Position Overview
The Director of Data Platform Governance is responsible for establishing, operating, and continuously improving the Digital Technology governance capabilities that ensure Enterprise Data Platform and related governance tooling ecosystem are controlled, integrated, secure, scalable, traceable, and fit for enterprise use. This includes platform governance standards, certified EDP table usage, metadata, catalog, lineage, data quality monitoring, lifecycle controls, automation, bots, agents, and other tools and services that support governed data creation, certification, publication, and consumption.
The role provides DT leadership for the technical enablement, enterprise integration, architecture and security alignment, platform controls, and operational reliability of this tooling ecosystem. SimpleMDG is a key Data Governance capability sitting on top of SAP, and the Director ensures it is integrated and governed consistently with EDP, SAP, downstream platforms, and other governance-enabling tools across the enterprise technology landscape. The Director also works closely with Technology Architects to ensure proper data flow, lineage, traceability, and integration patterns across the Enterprise Data Platform.
The Director works in close alignment with Business Transformation Data Governance through a shared agenda, agreed priorities, and clear ownership boundaries. Business Transformation Data Governance and business data owners remain accountable for business definitions, semantic layer, approval workflow design, mandatory business rules, reference data certification, stewardship logic, and business adoption, while DT ensures those decisions can be embedded consistently across platforms, workflows, tools, certified data assets, data products, and consumption layers.

Key Responsibilities

1. Enterprise Data Platform Governance and Certified Data Consumption
Establish, operate, and continuously improve DT governance standards for the Enterprise Data Platform, ensuring that data products are created and consumed using certified EDP tables where available.
Define platform-level controls, metadata, lineage, traceability, catalog, and data product governance expectations for EDP assets and consumption layers.
Partner with Business Data Governance and DT delivery teams to embed certified data consumption, lineage, controls, and governance checkpoints into delivery standards and ways of working.
Work with Technology Architects to ensure proper data flow, integration patterns, certified consumption paths, lineage, and traceability across the Enterprise Data Platform.
2. Governance Tooling Ecosystem Enablement
Provide DT leadership for the implementation, integration, controls, security, scalability, and operational reliability of the governance tooling ecosystem, including SimpleMDG, metadata and catalog solutions, lineage tools, data quality monitoring, automation, bots, agents, and related platform services.
Ensure governance tools are connected appropriately across SAP, EDP, downstream platforms, workflows, and consumption layers so that business-approved governance decisions can be executed consistently.
Maintain clear ownership boundaries by enabling business-led configuration decisions while ensuring the technical design, integration, access, auditability, and sustainability of the tools.
3. Master Data Platform Enablement and Enterprise Integration
Support business-led master data governance model by ensuring master data capabilities are technically enabled, integrated, secure, scalable, and aligned with enterprise architecture and data platform standards.
Ensure governed and certified master data can be integrated, exposed, monitored, and consumed appropriately across SAP, SimpleMDG, EDP, downstream enterprise applications, and certified data products.
Maintain lineage, traceability, metadata, issue visibility, platform controls, and certified consumption paths for master data from source systems through EDP and downstream usage.
4. Data Quality Monitoring, Controls, and Issue Visibility
Enable data quality monitoring, profiling, dashboards, scorecards, preventative controls, and issue visibility across EDP and related governance tooling.
Ensure business-defined rules, thresholds, and quality expectations can be technically implemented, measured, and monitored across platforms and consumption layers.
Partner with BT Data Governance, business stewards, Data Product Owners, and DT teams to support root-cause analysis, remediation tracking, and continuous improvement of data quality controls.
5. Metadata, Catalog, Lineage, and Data Intelligence
Establish and operate technical metadata, catalog, lineage, discovery, classification, and transparency capabilities for EDP and related data assets.
Ensure BT-owned business definitions, glossary content, critical data elements, and certification decisions are made visible and usable through platform tools, catalogs, workflows, and data products.
Work with Technology Architects and EDP teams to maintain end-to-end lineage and traceability from source systems through certified EDP tables, data products, and consumption layers.
6. Data Lifecycle, Archiving Governance, Retention, and Platform Compliance Controls
Operate technical lifecycle, data archiving governance, retention, archival, disposition, and compliance controls for EDP and related data platforms in alignment with enterprise policy, legal, regulatory, audit, and information governance requirements.
Ensure enterprise data remains manageable, controlled, compliant, traceable, and cost-efficient throughout its lifecycle, including active use, retention, archiving, and disposition across platform and consumption layers.

Required Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Supply Chain, or related discipline.
• 12+ years of progressive experience in Data Management, Data Platforms, Master Data Management, or Enterprise Information Management
• 5+ years leading data platform or MDM organizations.
• Strong expertise in SAP Master Data structures and business processes.
• Hands-on experience implementing and operating SAP MDG and/or SimpleMDG.
• Experience leading enterprise data quality initiatives.
• Experience enabling governance operating models and stewardship programs through platform capabilities
• Strong understanding of ERP transformation programs.
• Experience managing enterprise-scale cross-functional initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications
The ideal candidate demonstrates strong expertise in:

• Enterprise Data Platform governance, including certified data assets, governed consumption layers, platform standards, controls, and auditability.
• Data product and certified consumption governance, including ownership visibility, certification practices, guardrails, and governance checkpoints across data products and analytics use cases.
• Metadata, catalog, lineage, and data intelligence capabilities, including traceability, classification, discovery, and transparency across source systems, EDP, data products, and consumption layers.
• Data quality monitoring and control frameworks, including profiling, dashboards, scorecards, preventative controls, issue visibility, and remediation tracking.
• SAP, SimpleMDG/SAP MDG, and master data platform enablement, including integration across SAP, EDP, enterprise applications, analytics platforms, and downstream consumption layers.
• Enterprise integration and lifecycle governance, including source-to-consumption data flows, integration patterns, retention, archiving, compliance, and platform controls.
• Governance-enabling tooling and enterprise transformation, including workflow automation, bots, agents, metadata/catalog tools, lineage tools, data quality platforms, ERP transformation, and enterprise-scale data platform change.
• Critical enterprise data domains and operating models, including supply chain, customer, commercial, and other core data domains, with clear distinction between business-owned governance decisions and DT-owned platform enablement.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

• Pragmatic execution, solves complex business and data problems and turns governance concepts into measurable results.
• Business process orientation, understands how trusted data supports operational execution, performance, analytics, and decision-making.
• Enterprise mindset, connects platform governance, certified data consumption, and data quality to business outcomes and transformation priorities.
• Influential leadership, builds alignment across Business Transformation, Digital Technology, Data Product Owners, architects, and senior stakeholders.
• Change and adoption focus, drives practical adoption of governance standards, platform controls, tooling, and ways of working.
• Continuous improvement discipline, improves data quality, platform reliability, governance effectiveness, and operational efficiency.
